item.title: UIC Research: A Cancer Drug That Treats Herpes, Too | Newswise
item.description: UIC researchers have successfully repurposed an FDA-approved cancer drug, doxorubicin, to treat drug-resistant strains of herpes. Their work appears in the journal Drug Resistance Updates.

item.title: Hackensack Meridian Pascack Valley Medical Group Welcomes Dr. Liby Mathew | Newswise
item.description: Pascack Valley Medical Center is pleased to welcome Liby Mathew, M.D., to its internal medicine team. Dr. Mathew brings years of experience in adult primary care, providing preventive services, routine health screenings, and comprehensive management of chronic medical conditions.

item.title: Dana-Farber Team Develops Open-Access Predictive Tool to Improve Monitoring of Smoldering Multiple Myeloma | Newswise
item.description: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators have developed an online, easy-to-use tool that more accurately predicts when a precursor blood condition called smoldering multiple myeloma is likely to turn into active cancer than existing predictive models.

item.title: The Wired Belts Are the New Rust Belts | Newswise
item.description: Digital Planet at The Fletcher School at Tufts University launches the American AI Jobs Risk Index, the first comprehensive framework ranking U.S. occupations, industries, metro areas, and states by their actual vulnerability — not just exposure — to AI-driven job displacement.

item.title: Institute for Policy Solutions to Host National Convening on U.S. Response to Opioid and Behavioral Health Crisis | Newswise
item.description: Inequities in the U.S. opioid and behavioral health crisis response continue to leave groups behind, even as overall opioid overdose deaths decline. A March 31 Washington, D.C., event hosted by the Institute for Policy Solutions at Johns Hopkins School of Nursing focuses on addressing these gaps.

item.title: ER Triage for Children’s Behavioral Health Too Often Wrong, Shows Bias | Newswise
item.description: In emergency medicine, triage differentiates patients who require immediate attention from those who can safely wait for care. When it comes to children’s mental or behavioral health, however, triage scores were found to be inaccurate in two-thirds of the cases when compared to the level of care the child actually received during their emergency visit, according to a new study published in JAMA Network Open.
